what: A small set of pairwise difficulty judgements on canonical guitar shapes, used as an external check on the target of P7. Every shape is written low E first, dash separated, the way a chord chart reads.
annotator: Claude Opus 5, the language model that wrote this prototype. Not a guitarist, and not a human annotator.
protocol: Only pairs of shapes that appear in beginner and intermediate method books were considered.

The answer follows written pedagogy, not anyone's playing: an open chord is easier than a barre chord; fewer fingers is easier than more; a smaller stretch is easier than a bigger one; a muted string inside the chord is harder than one at the edge; the same shape is harder at the first fret than further up the neck.
A pair whose answer could not be defended from those rules was left out rather than guessed.
Pairs that are arguable are marked confidence "low" and are reported separately from the headline number.
The annotations were written before any model was trained and before any measurement was run.
No absolute difficulty is claimed: every line says only which of two shapes is harder.
caveat: A guitarist's ranking would be a better reference. This is not a substitute for one, and a cost function that matches it is only shown to agree with a written rule book.
